result:
task: Revise W1-38's support so the template hook source's three guard lines are held to the kernel template's exit-mapping line and its four lifecycle lines to DEC-608's plain form, each line exactly (DEC-917, P-W2-65-4 (b)).
status: DONE. The commit exists and all 201 W1-38 cases pass (8 were failing before).
work_completed: The sandbox check passed: (a) failed as it should, with `OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system`, and (b) worked, giving hash `1ae28402a109` with refresh exit 0. Identity matched the brief: `independent-test-designer` / `DAEO-e82f`, `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-65`, `w2/W2-65`, head `780b7569`. In the support, `expected_command_line` now gives a guard event (`GUARD_EVENTS` = PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure) the kernel template's own line for that event, read from its settings file. It gives a lifecycle event (`LIFECYCLE_EVENTS` = SessionStart, Stop, PreCompact, SubagentStop) `PLAIN_FORM` with the entry's own program, still found through `own_program` (exactly one program, by its whole file name). Any other event fails. `PLAIN_FORM_AS_WORDED` is quoted from DEC-608, with a comment giving its source. `kernel_form` is kept for the three guard lines only. In the test file, `KERNEL_EVENTS`/`OTHER_EVENTS` are now DEC-917's two named groups. `test_the_kernel_template_s_command_lines_share_one_form` now checks four things: the kernel registers exactly the three guard events; the source holds exactly the seven events; the three guard lines still share one form that names no program and is not the plain form; and the plain form names no program and has one place for it. The module docstring, the case docstrings and the failure messages now state DEC-917's two forms. Each changed part carries "Revised after implementation (Rewrite-Reason: DEC-917)". The product-package and containment cases are unchanged, and no case was renamed.
files_changed: tests/acceptance/W1-38/w1_38_hooks_support.py; tests/acceptance/W1-38/test_w1_38_hooks_command_line.py
evidence: Commit `c7eb7ee78e3d` with trailers Task: DAEO-e82f, Role: independent-test-designer, Implements: DEC-917, Rewrite-Reason: DEC-917, Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. 100 lines added, 41 removed. `git log --oneline -2`: `c7eb7ee78e3d DAEO-e82f (W2-65): W1-38 holds the three guard lines to the kernel template's exit-mapping line and the four lifecycle lines to DEC-608's plain form (DEC-917)` / `780b7569bbde W2-65 (DAEO-e82f): merge w2/integrate (fa53ba34) for run 3: …`. `git status --short` after the commit shows only untracked entries: `pytest-of-usain/`, `docs/source` and `.bash_profile .bashrc .gitconfig .gitmodules .idea .mcp.json .profile .ripgreprc .vscode .zprofile .zshrc`; nothing modified or staged. `gov.__file__` line: `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-65/src/gov/__init__.py`. Hooks check: `/home/usain/Dynamic-Agentic-Engineering-OS/.git/hooks` holds only `*.sample` files. Bite check: I ran a throwaway `python3 -B -c` that imports the support and calls `expected_command_line`, with no file written. It printed `SessionStart expected: python3 "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/governance/kernel/hooks/sessionstart.py" | == plain: True`, and the same for Stop (`stop.py`), PreCompact (`precompact.py`) and SubagentStop (`subagentstop.py`). For each lifecycle event it printed `exit-mapping line under <event> accepted? False` and `prefixed plain line accepted? False`; a line naming `precompact.py` under Stop/SessionStart/SubagentStop gives an expected line other than that event's plain line (False). For the guard events: `PreToolUse expected == kernel line: True | plain line for pretooluse.py accepted? False`, and the same for PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure (`posttooluse.py`, False). `unknown event: refused: Notification: Notification is neither a guard event … nor a lifecycle …`. `two programs: refused: Stop: the command line … names [stop.py, precompact.py]…`. Collect-only last line: `16506/16508 tests collected (2 deselected) in 7.26s`, no collection error.
tests: Before: `tests/acceptance/W1-38`, `8 failed, 193 passed in 188.59s (0:03:08)`. Because `-rs` hid the failing names, I took them from a re-run of `test_w1_38_hooks_command_line.py` alone with `-rfs` (`8 failed, 11 passed in 6.78s`): `TestGeneratedCommandLines::test_the_generated_command_line_has_the_kernel_template_s_form[SessionStart|Stop|PreCompact|SubagentStop]` and `test_the_source_s_command_line_is_the_kernel_template_s_form[SessionStart|Stop|PreCompact|SubagentStop]`. After: `tests/acceptance/W1-38`, `201 passed in 181.93s (0:03:01)`. Collect-only over `tests`: 16506/16508 collected, no error.
discoveries: (1) Before my change, `test_the_kernel_template_s_command_lines_share_one_form` was already green: the three kernel guard lines share one exit-mapping form. Only the lifecycle lines' derivation was broken. (2) `gov retrieve` was used once, for DEC-917 / W1-38's two forms. It returned no evidence (`stopping_reason: FACET_UNAVAILABLE`, lexical and semantic both "stale"), so I read the register entries and W1-38's files directly. (3) Untracked dotfiles (`.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.mcp.json`, `.idea`, `.vscode`, …) and `docs/source` show in this worktree, apparently the sandbox's placeholder mounts. I left them untouched and uncommitted. (4) Read refusals met: 0.
risks: (1) The check of which program belongs to which event is unchanged. A lifecycle line in plain form that names another kernel program would pass these command-line cases, as before; the any-folder cases hold each program's own answer, as W1-38's README states. (2) The case names `test_the_kernel_template_s_command_lines_share_one_form` and `…has_the_kernel_template_s_form` are kept, so ratchet lists and README references don't break, but their names now say less than their docstrings.
lessons: The plain form is now a literal in the support (`PLAIN_FORM_AS_WORDED`). If DEC-608's plain form ever changes again, that literal changes with the decision. The guard lines are still read from `template/governance/kernel/settings.json` at test time.
proposed_decisions: none
unresolved: W1-38's README is not named in the ticket body, so I left it. These lines are now stale: 343–345 (the seven lines held to DEC-608's one form); 352–357 (the four other events held to the kernel's form with their program put in); 358–360 (the shared form held because the four are read from it); 367 (the form case described as only "keeps the reading honest"); 369 (the four lifecycle generated lines "have the same form" as the kernel's); 370 (the seven source strings in one form). `tests/acceptance/W2-59/README.md` lines 265–268 may also need a look; I did not change them.
recommended_next_action: The lead verifies `c7eb7ee78e3d` with a run of `tests/acceptance/W1-38`, and has the two stale README passages updated by whoever owns W1-38's README.
